Pendize, early 14c., from Anglo-French pentiz, a shortening of Old French
apentis “attached building, appendage,” from Medieval Latin appendicium,
from Latin appendere “to hang”(see append). Modern spelling is from c.
English house (the meaning at that time was “attached building with a
sloping roof or awning”). Originally a simple structure (Middle English

homilies describe Jesus’ birthplace in the manger as a “penthouse”);
meaning “apartment or small house built on the roof of a skyscraper” first
recorded 1921, from which time dates its association with luxury.
